_readme: Anti-ratchet baseline for inline `# nosemgrep` suppressions.
An inline suppression silences a real security finding at one source site.
The accepted-risk register (shipwright_accepted_risks.yaml) deliberately has
NO target for it, because an offline reconciler would have to mirror Semgrep
and would drift, and because the register's defining field -- `expires` -- does
not fit a permanent false positive. That decision is recorded in
iterate-2026-08-05-inline-suppression-ratchet. THIS file is the control that
stands in its place.
The rule: measured sites for a rule may not EXCEED `max_sites`. A rule with no
entry at all blocks too, so a new suppression cannot arrive unrecorded. So does a
file that could not be read -- a partial count is a bypass, not a warning.
A count that SHRINKS is advisory: tighten `max_sites` to lock the improvement in.
The ONE reduction that blocks is a rule suppressed NOWHERE -- a `dead` entry.
Nothing in the tree corresponds to it any more, so it can never again be checked
against the thing it describes; delete it in the same change that removes the
last site. (This is the register's own STALE, under another name.)
To add a suppression you must, in the same change: raise `max_sites`, and cite
a `rationale_ref` NAMING a recorded decision -- an ADR number, an
iterate-YYYY-MM-DD-slug run id, or a #NNN issue/PR. Prose like 'TODO' is
rejected. Enforced by shared/tests/test_inline_suppressions_repo_guard.py.
Counts come from git-tracked source only -- prose and JSON/JSONL are excluded,
because a suppression comment cannot be in effect there. Check locally with:
uv run shared/scripts/tools/inline_suppressions_cli.py check --project-root .

rules.statement: Not a security finding: the rule flags Popen's `encoding`/`errors` kwargs as unavailable before Python 3.6. This project requires 3.11+ (pyproject.toml), so the incompatibility it warns about cannot occur.
Sibling of Popen1 and suppressed at the same two sites for the same reason: a pre-3.6 compatibility warning on a codebase pinned to 3.11+.

Every urllib call site here takes an operator-supplied configuration URL -- the deploy target, the smoke-test target (two sites), the dev-server health probe, the performance-budget probe, and the OpenRouter review endpoint -- never user input reaching the process from outside the repo. The rule flags any non-literal URL and cannot distinguish a config-derived one from an attacker-derived one.

The ADR-044/045 shared-leaf loader imports first-party sibling modules by computed name. Every site constrains the name to a hard-coded allowlist of first-party identifiers before importing; none accepts an externally-supplied module name.

The test runner executes a command string from the version-controlled shipwright profile (testing.commands.*), which is project-internal configuration. Shell semantics are required because those profile entries are written as shell command lines.
